summary: Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Kunzang Pelden, and Jigdrel Changchub Dorje, and taught Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and several other prominent students.

Domenico Pezzi (1844–1905) worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Turin (~1861–1865) under Giovanni Flechia, whom he succeeded in 1891, holding various faculty appointments in grammar and comparative linguistics there from 1871 onward.

Dominic Goodall is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his D.Phil. at Oxford (1995) under Alexis Sanderson and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He held fellowships at Oxford, lectured at EPHE (2005), and became a professor at EFEO in 2000.

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen Christina Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chönam. He held a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).

Dominik Haas specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna (2018–2022) under Marion Rastelli. His posts include lecturer at Vienna (2023) and postdoctoral researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2024).

Dominik Schröder (1910–1974) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He earned an M.A. at Fu Jen and a Ph.D. at Frankfurt (1949–1951) under Wilhelm Schmidt, later teaching at SVD St. Augustin and Nanzan University (1960–1969).

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist who earned his DPhil at Oxford (1978–1982). He held long-term posts at the Wellcome Institute/Trust (~1984–2002) and UCL (2002–2009), followed by appointments at the University of Vienna (2009–2014) and University of Alberta (2015–2024).

Dominique Sportiche (born 1952) is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He joined the faculty of the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1987 and taught Edward Garrett.

Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1990–1993) and served as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman (born 1939) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, and served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Richmond College, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and under George Uglow Pope and Wilhelm Geiger. He served as Ceylon government epigraphist (~1899–1929) and at the University of London (~1918–1930).

Donald A. Ringe (born 1954) is a linguist and Indologist. He earned an MPhil at Oxford and a PhD at Yale (~1976–1984) under Warren Crawford Cowgill. After teaching at Bard College (1983–1985), he joined the University of Pennsylvania faculty in 1985.

Donald E. Gjertson (born 1944) is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford (~1968–1975) under John Ching-yu Wang and Akira Takeda, and served on the faculty at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1976–2011).

Donald Eric Capps (1939–2015) was a religious studies scholar. Educated at Yale and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. ~1965–1970), he taught at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University before serving as William Harte Felmeth Professor at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).

Donald Ferguson (1853–1910) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. His education included studies at Denmark Hill Grammar School, Regent's Park College, and University College London.

Donald Harper is a sinologist who taught Zhiru Shi. He held a post at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and serves as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer (born 1934) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Mentored by Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai, he held long-term posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–1993) and served as a Distinguished Visiting Fellow at Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene (1922–2019) was a Japanologist. He studied at Columbia University (~1938–1951) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University from 1955.

Donald Phillip Verene (born 1937) is a philosopher who studied at Knox College and Washington University in St. Louis (doctorate ~1959–1964). He served as Chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College, Oxford, and Sapienza University.
